findings.claim: Strategy holds 845,256 bitcoin against software revenue of $122.37m in Q2 2026 and $124.3m in Q1 2026 (FY2025: $477m). The operating business is roughly 0.7% of the enterprise; the equity is a claim on an asset, not on an operating margin.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Strategy holdings following the 2026-08-31 purchase of 4,600 BTC; Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 results; FY2025 10-K

findings.claim: The reflexive issuance loop reversed in 2026. mNAV peaked at 3.89x in November 2024 and fell below 1.0 for the first time this cycle in late June 2026, at which point ATM issuance became dilutive to bitcoin per share and Strategy paused open-market bitcoin purchases for roughly ten weeks, resuming only on 2026-08-31.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: CoinDesk 2026-06-27 on enterprise mNAV below 1; mnav.com and Investing.com readings of 1.13-1.16x, 2026; market reporting on the purchase pause and its resumption

findings.claim: Strategy raised $8.41bn of gross ATM proceeds in Q2 2026 and a further $1.28bn between 1 and 26 July 2026, after raising $25.3bn in calendar 2025 (the largest US equity issuance for a second consecutive year) and $11.68bn in the first four months of 2026 (the largest US equity issuance of 2026).
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m ATM gross proceeds, Q2 2026
findings.source: Strategy Q2 2026 10-Q; Q1 2026 results, 2026-05-05; FY2025 disclosure

findings.claim: STRC's dividend rate is reset monthly by the board in increments of up to 0.25% to keep the stock trading at its $100 stated amount, with a contractual one-way ratchet that adds 0.5 percentage points (about $53m a year) if STRC trades below $95 and cannot be reversed if the price recovers. The rate has gone from 9.00% at listing in July 2025 to 11.50% in spring 2026 to 12.00% in September 2026, with STRC trading below par.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: Strategy STRC information page and 424B5 prospectus terms; company rate announcements July 2025 - September 2026; CoinDesk 2026-06-01; news.bitcoin.com on the 12% hold

findings.claim: Preferred dividends were $400.7m in Q2 2026, a $1.60bn annual run-rate, against total company revenue of roughly $495m for FY2026E - the fixed cash cost of the capital structure is about 3.2x total revenue.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The entire six-year bitcoin programme is approximately 2% above cost: 845,050 BTC acquired for $63.73bn, an average of $75,417 per bitcoin, against roughly $77,000 today - a cumulative gain of about $1.34bn. At the 2026-06-30 quarter end the position was below cost, with bitcoin at roughly $58,700.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Strategy holdings disclosure following the 2026-08-31 purchase; bitcoin price 2026-09-11 per Fortune and Yahoo Finance; Q2 2026 results showing holdings market value falling from $51.6bn at 2026-03-31 to $49.7bn at 2026-06-30

findings.claim: Treasury and IRS interim guidance issued 2025-09-30 allows a corporation to disregard unrealised gains and losses on digital assets when computing adjusted financial statement income for the 15% corporate alternative minimum tax. Strategy does not expect to be subject to CAMT on unrealised bitcoin gains, removing a multi-billion-dollar liability that would have begun in 2026.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: Treasury/IRS interim guidance 2025-09-30; Strategy 8-K response; The Block 2025-10

findings.claim: MSCI declined on 2026-01-15 to exclude digital-asset treasury companies from its Global Investable Market Indexes, deferring exclusions and size changes and opening a broader consultation on non-operating companies. Strategy was 74.5% of the $113bn of affected float-adjusted market cap; estimated forced outflows had ranged from $8.8bn (JPMorgan) to $15bn.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.unit: USD m estimated outflows avoided (JPMorgan estimate)
findings.source: MSCI consultation outcome, January 2026; Strategy letter of 2025-12-10 signed by Saylor and Le; Bitcoin Magazine and Crowdfund Insider reporting

findings.claim: Strategy remains excluded from the S&P 500 - the index committee will not admit a company whose income is pure asset exposure, and GAAP losses fail the earnings test - while retaining its Nasdaq-100 membership at the annual reconstitution. The largest passive bid available to a US large cap is structurally closed to it.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: S&P Dow Jones index committee decisions reported 2026; Nasdaq-100 reconstitution reporting, 2026

findings.claim: S&P Global Ratings assigned Strategy a B- issuer credit rating with a stable outlook on 2025-10-27, citing high bitcoin concentration, narrow business focus, weak risk-adjusted capitalization and low US dollar liquidity, and stated an upgrade is unlikely within twelve months.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE
findings.source: S&P Global Ratings, 2025-10-27; CoinDesk, The Block and Benzinga reporting

findings.claim: Michael Saylor no longer holds majority voting control: it fell below 50% on or shortly after 2024-11-12 because ATM issuance made Class A voting power exceed Class B. As at 2026-04-01 there were 326,581,627 Class A shares (1 vote) and 19,640,250 Class B shares (10 votes), giving Class B 37.6% of votes, now nearer 35% on a ~384m share count. Strategy no longer qualifies for the Nasdaq controlled-company exemption.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: % of votes held by Class B at 2026-04-01
findings.source: Strategy 2026 definitive proxy statement, share counts as at 2026-04-01; company 8-K disclosure of November 2024 on loss of majority voting control

findings.claim: Every convertible note in the structure is far out of the money: the 2029 notes convert at $672.40 and the 2030 notes at $433.43 against a $128.48 share price. None will convert to equity; all are debt to be refinanced or repaid in cash. Strategy repurchased and cancelled $1.50bn of 2029 notes for $1.38bn on 2026-05-19, leaving $1.50bn outstanding.

findings.claim: Cost of equity derived at 18.0%: risk-free 4.79% plus an equity beta of approximately 2.9 against a 4.5% equity risk premium. The beta is structural rather than regressed - the common is a roughly 1.37x levered claim on bitcoin, whose realised volatility is a multiple of the equity market's.

risks.text: Strategy is a price-taker on both sides of its only spread: it takes the bitcoin price on the asset side and the STRC market's required yield on the liability side
The cost of capital ratchets one way. STRC has gone 9.00% to 11.50% to 12.00% in fourteen months, with a contractual +0.5% trigger below $95 that cannot be reversed

conclusions: Strategy is a price-taker on both sides of its only spread. It takes the bitcoin price on the asset side and the STRC market's monthly reset on the liability side. There is no pricing power anywhere in the structure.

The reflexive flywheel reversed in June 2026: mNAV fell below 1.0 for the first time this cycle, issuance became dilutive to bitcoin per share, and the ATM stopped for ten weeks. The mechanism that created the premium requires the premium to exist.

The cost of capital ratchets and does not un-ratchet: STRC 9.00% to 12.00% in fourteen months with an irreversible trigger below $95, against a preferred dividend run-rate of $1.60bn a year on total revenue of about $495m.
Six years and $63.73bn of bitcoin purchases have produced a gain of roughly 2%: average cost $75,417 against about $77,000 today, and the position was below cost at the last quarter end.

The statutory news was good and it did not matter. CAMT relief removed a multi-billion tax liability and MSCI declined to exclude, yet the equity is roughly 65% below its 52-week high. The problem is arithmetic, not regulation.

Structural discount assessment: the premium was never a governance discount to be closed but an operating premium earned by accretive issuance. It returns only if a higher bitcoin price re-rates the equity above NAV first - which makes it a bet on bitcoin, not on Strategy.
thesisImpact: Establishes that this is not an operating company with a pricing problem but a leveraged, fee-bearing wrapper around an asset the buyer can own directly, whose one value-creating mechanism has stopped working while its cost of capital ratchets upward monthly and the asset return sits at zero. Phase 2 must size the asset and the cost of carrying it; Phase 3 must find the cash for $1.60bn of annual preferred dividends with the ATM shut; Phase 4 must test whether the levered wrapper beats owning the asset directly.
